predecessors.name: muttaraiyar
predecessors.text: Thanjavur and the Kaveri delta around it, captured from the Muttaraiyar c.

successors.name: Pandya Empire (Second Pandyan Empire)
successors.text: the Chola country, which the Pandyas had overrun by 1250 and which ended with Rajendra III c.

ledger.x: 848: Vijayalaya founds the Chola Empire in the Thanjavur country.
c. 850: Vijayalaya takes Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyar. 'in c. 850, captured Thanjavur from Muttarayar'.
897: Aditya I invades Tondai Nadu and ends Pallava rule.

c. 897: Aditya I is said to hold Kongu. The page says he 'conquered the Kongu Nadu region' and gives no year; 897 is bridged from the Tondai Nadu campaign and from the pandya-dynasty dossier, which dates the loss to c. 897 from its own page.

c. 910: Parantaka I takes Madurai. 'He captured the Pandyan capital, [Madurai], early in his reign'; he 'assumed the title Maturai Kontan (Capturer of Madurai) by the third year of his reign' (907 + 3). The page gives no calendar year for the capture; 910 is read from the regnal year.
c. 915: the Pandya war is decided at Vellur and the occupation of Madurai becomes annexation. 'The decisive battle appears to have taken place at Vellur around 915.'

c. 915: the Pandya country passes to the Cholas after Vellur ('around 915'). Cliopatria draws the south in the Chola shape only from 922; the pandya-dynasty dossier (another group) ends the Pandya state in 915 for the same reason.
944: Rashtrakuta Krishna III attacks the Chola north.
949: Takkolam decides the northern war.
949: the Cholas lose Tondaimandalam to the Rashtrakutas at Takkolam.

c. 967 (bridge): Parantaka II recovers Tondaimandalam. The page: Parantaka II 'recovered Tondaimandalam and defeated the Pandyas' and gives no year; Parantaka II reigned 957-970, and 967 is where the rashtrakuta-dynasty dossier ends Krishna III's reign and hold. Page silent on the year.
993: Rajaraja I conquers Anuradhapura.
998: Rajaraja I annexes Gangapadi, Nolambapadi and Tadigaipadi.
1001: Rajaraja I restores Saktivarman in Vengi, the start of the Chola protectorate over the Eastern Chalukyas.
1003: Rajaraja I opens the Ratta Padi campaign against the Western Chalukyas.

c. 1005: the Cholas hold Kollam (Venad) and southern Kerala. The Senur inscription lists 'defeating the formidable rulers of Kollam (Venad)'; 'The Chola subjugation of Kerala can be dated to the early years of the 11th century'; Kandalur Salai 'around 988' is a naval victory, not a gain.

c. 1010 (bridge): Rajaraja I's Kalinga invasion. 'The invasion of the kingdom of Kalinga occurred after the conquest of Vengi', marking 'the northern boundary of the Chola Empire at that time'. The page gives no year; Cliopatria draws the Chola shape to the Kalinga coast from 1010 and Rajaraja reigned to 1014. Page…
1017: Rajendra I completes the conquest of Sri Lanka.
1018: Rajendra I takes the Maldives and Lakshadweep.
1018: Rajendra I conquers the Chera Perumal kingdom of Kerala.
1019: Rajendra I conquers the Pandya country again.
1020: the Ratta Padi war ends with Maski.
1025: Rajendra I's naval expedition against Srivijaya and Kadaram.

c. 1025 (bridge): the seat moves to Gangaikonda Cholapuram. The page places the start of its building after the 1022 return from the Ganges and gives no founding year; the Kulottunga page calls it Kulottunga's capital. Page silent on the year.
1026: the raids end with the Srivijayan king in Chola hands.
1031: civil war in Vengi.
1045 (bridge): Rajadhiraja's Vengi expedition.
1070: Vijayabahu drives the Cholas out of Sri Lanka.
1070: Kulottunga I succeeds his cousin Athirajendra and the Later Cholas begin.
1075: the Eastern Chalukya line ends and the Vengi protectorate with it.
1075: Vengi becomes a Chola province.
1116: Vishnuvardhana takes Gangavadi.

c. 1118: Vengi falls to the Western Chalukyas. 'Around 1118, the Cholas lost control of Vengi to the Western Chalukya'; the Kulottunga page: 'a brief occupation of the Vengi territories between 1118 and 1126'.
1133: Vikrama Chola wins Vengi back.

c. 1177 (bridge): the Chola north shrinks to the Nellore latitude. Page silent on how Vengi left Chola hands; the Kulottunga page says only that the Pithapuram pillar inscription of Mallapadeva, dated 1202, shows 'the Vengi province became devoid of a ruler'. 1177 is where Cliopatria's Chola shape contracts and its…
1216: the Pandyas break the Chola south and west.
1216 (bridge inside Maravarman Sundara I's reign): the Chola king submits to the Pandyas.
1217: the Hoysalas break the Pandya overlordship.

c. 1241 (bridge): more of the Kaveri country goes to the Pandyas. Cliopatria's Pandya Empire row grows in 1241 and the Chola shape shrinks to 64,000 km2; the page gives no year for any campaign before Jatavarman Sundara I's accession in 1251. Page silent.
By 1250: the Pandyas reach the Chola north.

c. 1258-1260 (first year used): Rajendra III pays tribute to the Pandyas. 'Jatavarman Sundara I subdued Rajendra II around 1258-1260 CE and made him pay tribute'. Closed by the end of the dynasty in 1279.
1279: the tributary relation ends with the dynasty.
1279: the last Chola ruler is beaten and the dynasty ends.

wars.name: Chola conquest of the Pallava Tondai Nadu
wars.outcome: Aditya I invades Tondai Nadu in 897 and kills Aparajita; the Pallava country becomes Chola territory.

wars.name: Rashtrakuta-Chola war (Battle of Takkolam)
wars.outcome: Krishna III defeats the Cholas at Takkolam in 949 (Rajaraditya killed, per the Chola Empire page); the Cholas lose Tondaimandalam, recovered by Parantaka II.

wars.name: Chola raid on Sri Lanka under Parantaka I
wars.outcome: The Chola army 'invaded Sri Lanka around 946-947 AD, defeated the Sinhalese army' (Parantaka I page); no land is recorded as held.

wars.name: Chola conquest of Sri Lanka
wars.outcome: Anuradhapura conquered 993 (Rajaraja I); Ruhuna submits 1016; the Polonnaruwa kingdom is invaded 1017 and Mahinda V is carried to India (died 1029).

wars.name: Rajaraja I's conquest of Gangavadi and Nolambavadi
wars.outcome: Gangapadi, Nolambapadi and Tadigaipadi annexed in 998; Gangavadi 'conquered' by 1004.

wars.name: Chola-Western Chalukya wars of Rajaraja I and Rajendra I
wars.outcome: Rajaraja's Ratta Padi campaign (1003-04), raids in 1007 and c.

wars.name: Chola conquest of Kerala and the Pandya revival
wars.outcome: Kollam defeated by 1005 (Senur inscription), Kudamalai Nadu and the Chera Perumal and Pandya kingdoms conquered in 1017-1019.

wars.name: Chola Ganges expedition
wars.outcome: Rajendra's forces 'marched through Kalinga towards the Ganges river' in 1019; the 'Chola Indian Mainland expedition ended in 1022'.

wars.name: Chola invasion of Srivijaya
wars.outcome: Kadaram (Kedah) and Sri Vijaya taken in 1023 (Rajendra page); 'The Chola south-east Asian expedition ended in 1024', but the same page and the Chola invasion of Srivijaya page date the crossing and the invasion to 1025 (infobox 1025-1026), when the Srivijayan…

wars.name: Vengi succession wars
wars.outcome: After Vimaladitya's death in 1021 the throne is disputed; Vijayaditya drives Rajaraja Narendra out in 1031; Chola expeditions of 1035 and 1044-45; Someshvara I attacks Vengi 'and then the Cholas in 1054'.

wars.name: Kulottunga I's Kalinga and Pandya wars
wars.outcome: Kalinga conquered before 1096 (first war), a second invasion later; Pandya revolts suppressed c.

wars.name: Chola-Western Chalukya war of 1075-76 and the Vengi occupation
wars.outcome: 1075-76: Chalukya incursion into Chola territory, battle in the Kolar district; Vengi occupied 1118-1126; Battle of the Godavari by 1133.

wars.name: Hoysala conquest of Gangavadi
wars.outcome: Vishnuvardhana's victory over the Cholas at Talakadu in 1116; the Cholas lose the Gangavadi districts.

wars.name: Pandya conquest of the Chola country
wars.outcome: Maravarman Sundara Pandya I sacks Uraiyur and Thanjavur and drives Kulottunga III into exile (1215-16); in 1217 Veera Ballala II 'defeated the aggressive Pandya' and Rajaraja III is restored.

wars.name: Pandya-Hoysala-Chola wars and the end of the Cholas
wars.outcome: Jatavarman Sundara Pandya I reaches Nellore and exacts tribute from the last Chola c.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages opened: frontiers are inscriptional claims and campaign limits (the Tungabhadra, the Kalinga coast, the Pandya country).
